Our Process

How We Handle Home Renovations in Toronto

Every home renovation we complete in Toronto follows the same six-phase process, so you always know exactly where your project stands.

01

Complimentary Consultation

We meet at your Toronto home, review existing conditions, and discuss your renovation goals, wish list, and budget. You get an honest early read on feasibility and realistic cost ranges, without any obligation.

02

Design & Material Selection

Our in-house architects produce drawings and our interior designers walk you through finish options, cabinetry, tile, countertops, fixtures, and flooring — with full design services included.

03

Fixed-Price Quote

Once the design is approved, we issue a fully itemized fixed-price contract. Every line — labour, materials, permits — is listed before you sign. Your price is locked. No cost-plus billing.

04

Permits & Approvals

For any renovation requiring a permit, we handle the full City of Toronto building permit application, structural drawings, and all inspector coordination, start to finish.

05

Construction & Trade Management

Our on-site supervisor coordinates all trades and performs documented quality checks at each milestone. Your dedicated coordinator sends regular updates so you always know where things stand.

06

Final Walkthrough & Handover

We walk through every detail together, address any deficiencies on the spot, and hand your renovated home over with full documentation — warranties, permits, and maintenance guides included.

Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

In the Toronto market, the highest return on investment comes from projects that increase functional square footage or improve energy efficiency.

  • Legal basement suites: adding a rental suite or secondary dwelling unit is the top value-adder, given Toronto’s housing demand.
  • Kitchen refreshes: minor to mid-range updates (new counters, cabinet refacing, energy-efficient appliances) typically outperform major luxury guts.
  • Bathroom upgrades: modernizing fixtures or adding a second bathroom to a single-bath home significantly boosts resale appeal.
  • Energy efficiency: heat pumps, triple-pane windows, and high-performance insulation are increasingly attractive to buyers facing rising utility costs.
  • Curb appeal: a new front door, professional landscaping, or updated siding offers high impact for a relatively low investment.

In 2026, a full house renovation in Toronto typically costs between $150 and $450 per square foot, depending on the age of the home and the quality of finishes. For a standard 1,500 sq ft detached home, budget between $200,000 and $600,000+.

  • Basic / cosmetic ($150–$200 per sq ft): painting, new flooring, and mid-range kitchen or bath refreshes without moving walls.
  • Mid-range ($200–$350 per sq ft): layout changes, custom cabinetry, upgraded electrical and plumbing, and high-quality materials such as quartz and hardwood.
  • High-end / full gut ($350–$500+ per sq ft): structural alterations, luxury finishes, smart home integration, and modern energy-efficiency upgrades.

Local tip: factor in 13% HST, City of Toronto permit fees (which can range from $2,000 to $10,000+ for major work), and a 15% contingency fund for the hidden surprises common in older Toronto properties.

The timeline depends on the scope of work and the City’s permit approval speed. On average:

  • Cosmetic refresh (1–2 months): surface-level updates like painting, new flooring, and lighting.
  • Kitchen or bathroom remodel (3–5 months): includes design and ordering custom cabinetry, which carries 8–12 week lead times.
  • Basement finishing (4–6 months): standard finishing is relatively quick, but a legal secondary suite or underpinning extends this significantly.
  • Full house gut or major addition (9–15+ months): these projects require extensive architectural drawings and structural permits.

The Toronto factor: budget 3–6 months before construction for design and City of Toronto approvals. If your project requires a Committee of Adjustment hearing for zoning variances, add another 3–5 months to the pre-construction phase.

Living through a renovation is a test of patience. Depending on which parts of the house you are renovating, we recommend:

  • Setting up a “mini-kitchen”: move your microwave and coffee maker to a clean room.
  • Decluttering: move all furniture and breakables out of the work zone.
  • Dust protection: make sure your contractor uses plastic sheeting and HEPA filters.

Avoid these frequent pitfalls to keep your project on track and under budget:

  • Skipping the contingency fund. Unexpected issues like mould or faulty wiring often hide behind walls. Always set aside an extra 10–20% of your budget.
  • Hiring solely on price. The lowest bid often reflects a lack of insurance, subpar materials, or hidden fees.
  • Changing your mind mid-project. Scope creep is a timeline killer. Finalize fixtures and floor plans before the first hammer swings.
  • Over-improving for the area. If you plan to sell, make sure upgrades match the neighbourhood’s price point.
  • Neglecting lighting and outlets. Plan your electrical layout early so you aren’t stuck with extension cords in your new space.
  • DIY-ing the technical stuff. Leave structural work, plumbing, and electrical to licensed pros to keep your home up to code.

For targeted renovations — a bathroom, kitchen, or basement — yes, most homeowners remain in their home. We maintain clean, liveable conditions in unaffected areas. For full home renovations, some Toronto homeowners temporarily relocate. We give you an honest assessment of disruption levels during planning, before you sign anything.

It depends on scope. Cosmetic renovations — painting, flooring, cabinet swaps — typically don’t require a permit. Structural changes, wall removals, electrical upgrades, plumbing moves, and envelope changes require a City of Toronto building permit. We assess permit requirements for every project and manage all applications, submissions, and inspections entirely on your behalf.

Always check with your local building department first. Unpermitted work can complicate future home sales and may lead to fines.

Yes. For any home renovation in Toronto requiring a building permit, we handle the full process: assessing whether a permit is required, preparing and submitting the application, producing structural drawings where required, coordinating City inspectors throughout construction, and obtaining final sign-off at completion.
